haiku-low.q1: The indexer deletes that product's document by id, since archived is not active and only active products may appear in search.
haiku-low.q2: The older write is refused as a version conflict, counted in a metric, and not treated as an error, so the newer data stays.
haiku-low.q3: It retries only those documents, waiting 1 s, then 2 s, doubling up to 60 s. It never saves offsets past unacknowledged documents, so the consumer waits and the lag alert fires.
haiku-low.q4: It publishes the document with its error to catalog.products.dlq, raises an alert, and carries on. The DLQ write must succeed before offsets move past it.
haiku-low.q5: At 50 GB ops drops the slot to protect the primary, so changes after the drop are missing. Recovery is a full rebuild: recreate the slot, restart Debezium without snapshot, then rebuild.
haiku-low.q6: The alias products is moved atomically from products_v3 to products_v4 once the gate holds: under 5 s behind and count within 0.5% of the active count.
haiku-low.q7: Offsets are stored in Kafka. They are saved only after the index acknowledges the bulk writes covering them.
haiku-low.q8: Offsets were not saved, so it re-reads the batch. The version rule makes the repeated writes harmless.
haiku-low.q9: A second indexer group replays catalog.products from offsets at time S minus one minute, writing with commit_lsn versions. Replay waits until the backfill finishes, and conflicts below S are skipped.
haiku-low.q10: Bulk-copied documents carry version S, the WAL position recorded when the rebuild started.
haiku-low.q11: The old index's indexer group keeps running so products_v3 stays current, and rollback is moving the alias back. After 48 hours that group is stopped and products_v3 deleted.
haiku-low.q12: If the backfill dies, delete products_v4 and restart; if the gate never holds, alert with no switch. Search keeps using the old index throughout.

sonnet.q1: The document is deleted from the index (delete id with commit_lsn as version); a delete of a document that is not there counts as success.
sonnet.q2: The older write has a lower version than the stored one, so the index returns a version conflict. The change is skipped as stale and counted in a metric; it is not an error.
sonnet.q3: It retries just the failing documents, waiting 1 s, then 2 s, doubling up to a 60 s cap. It never saves offsets past an unacknowledged document. If failures continue, the consumer waits and the lag alert fires.
sonnet.q4: It is published with the error to the DLQ topic catalog.products.dlq, an alert is raised, and the indexer carries on. The DLQ write must succeed before offsets move past it.
sonnet.q5: At 50 GB ops drops the replication slot to protect the primary, so changes made after the drop are missing from the index. Recover with a full rebuild: first recreate the slot and restart Debezium without an initial snapshot, then start the rebuild, taking S after the slot exists.
sonnet.q6: The rebuild moves the alias products from the old index to the new one in one atomic step. This happens only when the gate holds. The new index must be under 5 s behind (the oldest unapplied event is under 5 s old, or there is none), and its document count must be within 0.5% of the count of active rows in Postgres. The check runs every minute.
sonnet.q7: The offsets are stored in Kafka, in a consumer group named after the index. They are saved only after the index acknowledges the batch's writes.
sonnet.q8: It re-reads the batch, because the offsets were not saved. The version rule makes the repeated writes harmless.
sonnet.q9: S, the WAL position and time, is recorded before the snapshot opens. After the backfill finishes, a second indexer group replays catalog.products from the offsets at the time of S minus one minute and writes to the new index with commit_lsn versions. Events with a version below S are skipped as conflicts, and later events are applied in order.
sonnet.q10: Version S, the WAL position recorded at the start of the rebuild.
sonnet.q11: The old index's indexer group keeps running for 48 hours, so the old index stays current. To roll back, move the alias back to it and no change is lost. After 48 hours the group is stopped and the old index is deleted.
sonnet.q12: Search is unaffected, because the alias still points at the old index, which stays live and untouched. If the backfill dies, delete the new index and restart. If the gate never holds, there is no switch and an alert is raised.
